items.title: FG disappointed as COP31 ends without political deal
items.description: By Folarin Kehinde The Federal Government has expressed disappointment over the failure of the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) to reach consensus on an overarching political agreement, describing the outcome as a setback for international climate cooperation. The Director-General of the National Council on Climate Change (NCCC), Dr Omotenioye Majekodunmi, said, however, that the development would not weaken Nigeria’s commitment to addressing climate change. Majekodunmi stated this in a statement published on the X handle of the NCCC following the conclusion of the conference in Antalya, Turkey. She acknowledged that progress was recorded on some negotiating issues but maintained that the absence of a comprehensive political agreement did not invalidate existing commitments under the Paris Agreement. “COP31’s failure to reach consensus on an overarching political outcome is deeply disappointing and represents a setback for international climate cooperation,” she said. Outlining Nigeria’s priorities, the NCCC director-general said the country would concentrate on implementing its Nationally Determined Contribution 3.0 (NDC 3.0), strengthening climate governance, mobilising investments and pursuing a just energy transition. “For Nigeria, our focus remains firmly on implementation. We will continue advancing our NDC 3.0, strengthening climate governance, mobilising investment and pursuing an orderly, just and nationally determined energy transition,” she said. Majekodunmi said the conference outcome had reinforced the need for climate commitments to be supported by credible financing, practical implementation strategies and recognition of the varying circumstances of countries. She reaffirmed Nigeria’s commitment to working with African partners and the international community to build consensus and accelerate global climate action. According to her, the country’s progress on climate action should not be measured solely by emissions reduction but also by its impact on job creation, business development, improved energy access and better livelihoods. The post FG disappointed as COP31 ends without political deal appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: From national service to future leadership: Why mentorship matters more than ever
items.description: Every year, thousands of talented graduates enter the workforce full of ambition, potential, and academic knowledge. Yet many quickly discover that success in the workplace requires much more than technical competence. The transition from university to professional life is one of the most significant shifts in a young person’s development. It is a period filled with uncertainty, self-discovery, and often an unspoken expectation to immediately “figure things out.” This is where mentorship becomes invaluable. Bridging the Gap Between Knowledge and Experience Universities play a critical role in building technical foundations. However, some of the most important professional skills are learned through experience. How to manage competing priorities and communicate with senior stakeholders. Even how to navigate setbacks, feedback, and workplace dynamics. These are lessons that cannot always be taught in a classroom. This gap between academic preparation and workplace expectations is particularly relevant in Ghana. National Service is intended, in part, to give graduates practical workplace exposure and help bridge the transition from tertiary education to employment. Mentors provide guidance that helps young professionals connect theory with practical application. They offer perspective, encouragement, and access to experiences that can accelerate learning. A National Imperative As organisations compete for talent, mentoring should no longer be viewed simply as a goodwill initiative. It should be considered a strategic investment. That need is increasingly recognised at the national level. In 2026, Ghana’s National Service Authority (NSA) and UNFPA Work Readiness and Leadership Training Programme were reported as targeting approximately 150,000 graduates annually, with training covering personal leadership, digital agility, civic education, health and rights, and global awareness. Structured mentoring can complement initiatives like these by providing what formal training alone cannot always offer: continuous and individualised guidance within the realities of the workplace. For employers, the opportunity goes beyond helping young professionals settle into their first roles. Effective mentorship can contribute to leadership development and build the capabilities organisations will need from their next generation of managers. A systematic review done in 2026, for example, found mentoring programmes beneficial for developing leadership competencies as well as participants’ personal and professional growth, although the evidence reviewed was specifically focused on managers in healthcare. Mentorship is a Two-Way Exchange One common misconception is that mentoring benefits only the mentee. In reality, the relationship can create value for mentors too. Research has specifically examined the career benefits associated with serving as a mentor, reinforcing the case for viewing mentoring as more than a one-directional transfer of knowledge. Mentors gain exposure to emerging perspectives, new ideas and the expectations of a changing workforce. Mentees gain access to experience, context and lessons that may have taken their mentors years to acquire. When approached intentionally, mentorship creates a cycle of learning that benefits individuals, organisations and ultimately society. Building the Next Generation The leaders who shape Ghana’s future are already among us. Many are currently serving as interns, trainees and National Service personnel. The question is whether we are creating environments that help them thrive. Ghana’s National Service system itself occupies an important position between tertiary education and employment, providing graduates with exposure to professional environments and practical experience. Mentorship offers organisations an opportunity to make that transition more deliberate, ensuring young professionals are not only given work to do, but also supported to understand how to work, how to grow and eventually how to lead. Mentorship cannot eliminate every challenge a young professional will face. However, it can ensure they do not face those challenges alone. The most enduring professional legacies are rarely measured only by what we achieve ourselves. They are also measured by the people we inspire, develop and empower to achieve even more . items.title: GISPA moves to strengthen industry collaboration and advocacy across Ghana’s digital sector
items.description: The Ghana Internet Service Providers Association (GISPA) is stepping up efforts to strengthen collaboration, policy engagement and collective advocacy across Ghana’s digital infrastructure ecosystem, as it seeks to build a more coordinated industry voice on issues shaping the country’s digital future. The renewed direction was underscored at an industry networking reception in Accra, which brought together key players across the sector, including Mobile Network Operators (MNOs), Internet Service Providers (ISPs), data centre operators and submarine cable companies. The gathering gave industry stakeholders a chance to reconnect, exchange perspectives, and identify shared priorities, reinforcing GISPA’s ambition to become a more inclusive and influential platform for engagement across Ghana’s wider digital communications and infrastructure landscape. Beyond its traditional role of representing Internet Service Providers, GISPA is seeking to deepen engagement across the wider digital infrastructure ecosystem, recognising the interconnected roles of connectivity providers, mobile network operators, data centres, international cable operators and other critical stakeholders. This renewed direction places greater emphasis on industry dialogue, policy engagement and collective representation on issues affecting the sustainability, competitiveness and growth of Ghana’s digital sector. “Ghana’s digital economy can only achieve its full potential when the industry works together. Our renewed direction is about building stronger relationships across the digital infrastructure ecosystem, identifying shared priorities and ensuring that GISPA provides a credible platform for dialogue, collaboration and collective advocacy. We want to see an industry that is not only growing but also working together to shape the policies and investments that will define its future”, Micheal K. K Nfodzo, GISPA President said. As Ghana advances its digital transformation ambitions and explores opportunities in artificial intelligence, digital services and the wider digital economy, GISPA believes that a stronger, more coordinated industry voice is essential. The event also reinforced the importance of stronger relationships between industry players and public-sector stakeholders, including the Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, the National Communications Authority (NCA), the Ghana Chamber of Telecommunications and other relevant regulatory and policy institutions. Several issues require sustained industry attention, including infrastructure investment, regulatory sustainability, taxation, interconnection, internet exchange development, international connectivity, competition and the affordability of digital services. Of particular importance is the need for a comprehensive review of the legislative and regulatory framework governing the digital communications industry. As Ghana continues to introduce and review legislation affecting the digital economy, the implications for industry players must be carefully assessed. This includes the cumulative impact of laws, regulatory obligations, taxes, levies and compliance requirements on investment, operational sustainability, competition, innovation and the affordability of digital services. GISPA believes that meaningful industry consultation and impact assessments should be integral to the legislative process, ensuring that policy and regulatory interventions support national digital ambitions while creating an enabling environment for sustainable private-sector investment and growth. “As an industry, we need a regulatory environment that recognises the realities of operating and investing in Ghana’s digital infrastructure. Policies and legislation must be informed by meaningful consultation with industry players and a clear understanding of their cumulative impact. A more coordinated approach will help create the right conditions for investment, innovation, competition and affordable digital services”, Kwadwo Ofei-Djan (KOD) Afriband Telecommunications Network, intimated. The Association is committed to facilitating constructive engagement between industry stakeholders, policymakers and regulators, ensuring that industry perspectives inform decisions affecting the sector’s future. As part of its forward agenda, GISPA will continue to strengthen its governance and institutional capacity, deepen member engagement, promote the development of the Ghana Internet Exchange (GIX) and pursue strategic partnerships that advance local internet interconnection and improve the resilience of Ghana’s digital infrastructure. The Association also intends to sustain engagement beyond formal meetings and conferences by creating opportunities for stakeholders to exchange ideas, identify shared priorities and develop practical solutions to common industry challenges. The message from the gathering was clear: Ghana’s digital future is a shared responsibility, and the industry is stronger when it speaks, engages and works together.

items.title: Ahmad Tibi et Mansour Abbas, deux visages de la lutte des Palestiniens d’Israël
items.description: Ils partagent une meme cause, mais pas la meme methode. Depuis les elections israeliennes du 27 octobre, Ahmad Tibi et Mansour Abbas incarnent deux voies pour les citoyens arabes d'Israel, descendants des Palestiniens restes sur place apres la creation de l'etat hebreu en 1948. Leur poids politique n'a jamais ete aussi important : leurs deux listes totalisent 19 des 120 sieges de la Knesset, au moment ou la formation d'un gouvernement se joue a quelques voix pres. Ahmad Tibi, medecin de formation et ancien conseiller de Yasser Arafat, est l'une des figures historiques de cette minorite, qui represente environ un cinquieme de la population israelienne. a la tete du parti Ta'al, integre a la Liste commune, il defend la reconnaissance des droits nationaux palestiniens et l'egalite civique. Sa formation, alliee a Hadash et Balad, dispose de 11 sieges. Oppose a Benjamin Netanyahou, Tibi se dit pret a soutenir de l'exterieur un cabinet conduit par Gadi Eisenkot, mais refuse d'entrer dans une coalition dont il contesterait la politique a Gaza et en Cisjordanie. S'opposer ou tenter d'imposer une nouvelle ligne depuis l'interieur Mansour Abbas privilegie la negociation avec le pouvoir. Chef de Ra'am, une formation issue de la mouvance islamiste, il a cree un precedent en 2021 en rejoignant la coalition de Naftali Bennett et Yaïr Lapid. Son objectif : obtenir des budgets pour les communes arabes, lutter contre la criminalite et ameliorer logements et infrastructures. Avec huit deputes elus en octobre, il souhaite retrouver une place dans les discussions gouvernementales, sans renoncer a defendre la creation d'un etat palestinien. Leur divergence pose une question fondamentale : faut-il peser sur les institutions de l'interieur ou defendre ses revendications depuis les bancs de l'opposition ? Dans les deux cas, l'equation reste delicate. Alors que les partis juifs hesitent a dependre de leurs voix, Tibi et Abbas cherchent a convertir une percee electorale historique en avancees concretes pour leur electorat.

items.title: SkyTrain trial adjourned as Solomon Asamoah seeks new lawyer
items.description: The Accra High Court has granted Solomon Asamoah, the first accused in the $2 million SkyTrain case, additional time to secure a new lawyer following the withdrawal of his previous counsel. Victoria Barth withdrew from the case on November 16, 2026, after disagreements with the court over the order requiring her client to open his defence before calling his witnesses. Before withdrawing, Ms Barth drew the court’s attention to two applications filed at the Court of Appeal and the Supreme Court challenging the directive. The trial court, however, declined to suspend proceedings pending the determination of the applications, prompting her to step down. Following her withdrawal, the court granted Mr Asamoah more time to arrange new legal representation before the trial resumes. The case concerns allegations of financial loss to the state arising from a proposed SkyTrain project. The trial is ongoing before the Accra High Court, where the court is hearing the case against the accused persons. The proceedings have been adjourned to allow Mr Asamoah to secure a new lawyer. The trial is expected to continue once his new legal representation is in place.

items.title: Bilawal calls for restoring supremacy of Parliament and trust in judiciary, electoral system
items.description: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Monday called for restoring the supremacy of the Parliament as well as trust in the judiciary and the electoral system. He made the remarks while addressing an event to mark the launch of the Sindh Youth Card. “To restore the trust of Pakistan’s youth, if any reset is to take place, it must be a democratic reset,” the party leader said. “If a democratic reset happens, then the people’s stake will remain, and through that reset, we must restore the supremacy of our Parliament. We must restore confidence in our judiciary, and the election system we have, we must restore trust in it now.” Bilawal’s remarks come as the debate over a “system reset” in the country has intensified over the past few months. In July, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi stirred a political storm by calling for the creation of new administrative units , arguing that the current system of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”. Last week, in a hard-hitting speech, the PPP chairman had asserted that the governance system had not collapsed, but was rather “made to collapse”. “Every child in this country hates corruption. The youth [of Pakistan] want to see a country where there is no corruption. They want it, and we also want to join together and build such a Pakistan,” he said. According to Bilawal, to achieve that objective, two things need to be done: first is to use modern digital technology, whether it is Youth Card or Kissan Card , and build systems in a way that shuts down avenues for corruption. “Along with that, we have to build a system that functions without discrimination,” he added. “Instead of taking revenge, [the system] works to fix our situation.” Bilawal stressed that the restoration of trust would have to be a “joint effort” — to restore the opposition’s trust in the government, the government’s trust in the opposition, and the public’s trust in the country’s system, its parliament, judiciary, media and the accountability system. He said if such conditions were created, Pakistan could achieve unity for the first time, enabling it to confront economic hardships, fallout due to war , terrorism , climate change -related disasters, or any crisis arising from artificial intelligence . “I know that a Pakistan that is united, we have the ability to face any crisis, any disaster, any catastrophe.” “At the same time, I fear that if we keep fighting among ourselves and remain divided further, and [spread hatred] in society instead of hope, then we will not have the capacity to face any crisis,” Bilawal added. “Then whatever happens to Pakistan, whatever negative consequences occur, the youth will hold us accountable, asking, ‘you were there, what did you do to save us from this trouble?’ And at least I want when that question is asked, I can proudly, with my head held high, say that my intentions were good,” the chairman further said. The Bhutto scion claimed he had poured his blood and sweat into resolving the nation’s issues. “I made this effort so conditions would be created in this country enabling us to serve you,” he said. “And if I succeed, then it will be for the benefit of Pakistanis, for the benefit of our country. Even if I fail, history will remember that a young man stood up and tried.” More to follow

Kenya: Moyale Emergency - Public Health Situation Analysis (PHSA)
items.description: Countries: Kenya, Ethiopia Source: World Health Organization Please refer to the attached file. Since 18 October 2026, there has been active conflict within the Oromia and Somali regions of Ethiopia. The conflict on the Ethiopian side of Moyale, has reportedly displaced approximately 60 000 people into Kenya, with registration continuing as new arrivals are reported. Although a ceasefire has reportedly held since 17 November, the security situation remains fragile, with cross-border humanitarian movements disrupted. A Government led assessment published 3 November 2026 found limited access to health care with 53% of all households (398/755) reporting that they cannot access nearby health centre. Households who reported inaccessible healthcare cited higher costs (49%) and drug stockouts (44%) as the drivers of inaccessibility. Marsabit is one of Kenya’s 23 Arid and Semi-Arid Lands (ASAL) counties and was already facing food insecurity before the influx, which compounds pressure on local resources. Humanitarian access to some border areas, including Somare, remains constrained. On 9 November, Kenya’s Prime Cabinet Secretary said Ethiopia had assured Kenya it is working to restore normalcy. Reports indicate that the root cause of clashes between rival forces are long-standing local disputes related to land ownership, governance, ethnic differences and political disagreements. Successful peace talks remain essential for people to return home safely. The United Nations is appealing for USD 8.9 million to address the most critical lifesaving needs for the next three months.

items.title: Katsina political rift: Calls grow for Radda, Masari to reconcile
items.description: By Fauziyya Lawal, Katsina The reported disagreement between Katsina State Governor, Dikko Umaru Radda, and the Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Political Matters, Alhaji Ibrahim Kabir Masari, has generated debate within political circles, with calls for dialogue to prevent the dispute from affecting the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the state. The disagreement has raised questions about the relationship between the two influential APC figures and its possible implications for party unity, particularly as political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections gather momentum. At the centre of the controversy are allegations of attempts to undermine the governor’s administration, disagreements over political billboards and questions surrounding the influence of federal political appointees in the state’s political affairs. In a circulating video, Governor Radda was heard expressing concerns about some individuals allegedly working from Abuja to undermine his administration, promising to provide further details at an appropriate time. However, the governor did not expressly identify Masari as one of the individuals he was referring to, making it premature to conclude that his remarks were directed at the presidential aide. Similarly, footage of the two politicians engaging cordially has circulated publicly, underscoring the need for caution in interpreting their relationship amid competing political narratives. Providing his account of the disagreement during an interview with BBC Hausa, Masari traced the development to the appearance of campaign billboards promoting Governor Radda and some of his political associates without the photograph of President Tinubu. According to him, he and other Katsina-born federal political appointees, including Minister of Housing and Urban Development, Muttaqa Rabe Darma, and Jabiru Tsauri, subsequently contributed money to produce alternative billboards featuring Tinubu, Vice-President Kashim Shettima, Governor Radda, former governors Aminu Bello Masari and Ibrahim Shehu Shema, alongside other political stakeholders. Masari also alleged that some of the billboards were destroyed, accusing the governor’s Chief Security Officer and Aide-de-Camp of involvement. He, however, acknowledged that he could not establish whether Governor Radda personally authorised the alleged destruction. The allegations have yet to be independently established, while clarification from the individuals accused would be necessary to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident. Beyond the billboard controversy, the disagreement has also been linked by political observers to developments within Katsina’s political structure, particularly the removal of Architect Ahmed Musa Dangiwa as Minister of Housing and Urban Development and his replacement with Darma. Dangiwa, a former Secretary to the Katsina State Government and political associate of Radda, had been regarded in some quarters as an important figure within the governor’s political circle. His replacement subsequently generated questions about political consultation, competing interests and the influence of different stakeholders in the state’s political affairs. Masari, however, reportedly denied influencing Dangiwa’s removal during his BBC Hausa interview, describing suggestions of his involvement as baseless. The distinction is important as speculation about political appointments and disagreements should not be presented as established facts without supporting evidence. The controversy has also brought renewed attention to the relationship between federal political appointees and elected officials in Katsina. While federal appointees have a legitimate role in promoting the political interests of the President and the ruling party, supporters of Governor Radda also have the right to publicise his administration’s achievements and political profile. The challenge, therefore, is how such activities can be coordinated without creating unnecessary competition or undermining party cohesion. Masari occupies a strategic position within the Presidency, while Radda has the constitutional responsibility of governing Katsina State. Their respective political responsibilities and networks could provide opportunities for stronger federal-state cooperation rather than rivalry. Masari has also publicly acknowledged Radda’s performance and achievements, expressing no regret over supporting his emergence as governor. He has further indicated that his concerns are directed at certain individuals around the governor rather than necessarily against Radda personally. These positions could provide an opening for dialogue if both parties are willing to address their differences. Reports have also indicated that President Tinubu intervened in the disagreement, directing his political adviser to engage relevant stakeholders and facilitate dialogue in Katsina. Such an intervention, if confirmed, could provide an opportunity to clarify the issues and address the concerns of the parties involved. The APC also faces the challenge of managing competing interests among elected officials, former governors, ministers, presidential aides and other influential stakeholders. Disagreements within political parties are not unusual, but their resolution through internal mechanisms and dialogue remains important to maintaining organisational cohesion. For Katsina, the implications extend beyond the relationship between the two politicians. With the 2027 general elections approaching, prolonged disagreements among influential APC stakeholders could deepen factional divisions, affect grassroots mobilisation and create opportunities for opposition parties. More importantly, the state has pressing development challenges requiring sustained attention from its political leadership. Security, education, healthcare, agriculture, infrastructure and employment generation remain important priorities across Katsina’s 34 local government areas. Political stakeholders could therefore channel their influence towards attracting federal support, strengthening governance and advancing development initiatives rather than allowing personal disagreements to dominate the political space. Neither Radda nor Masari stands to benefit significantly from an unresolved confrontation, particularly given their respective positions and political networks within the APC. Their cooperation could also help strengthen relations between the state government and federal political structures. Ultimately, the disagreement calls for restraint, transparency and constructive engagement among the parties involved. The priority should be to establish the facts surrounding the allegations, address genuine grievances and prevent political differences from escalating into wider divisions within the party. For Katsina, the overriding concern should be how political influence can be translated into better governance and tangible benefits for residents. The state’s interests should remain central to efforts to resolve the disagreement, with dialogue and cooperation taking precedence over factional considerations. The post Katsina political rift: Calls grow for Radda, Masari to reconcile appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Le journal de la présidentielle 2027 : le point sur les sondages, les candidats et les alliances
items.description: Les Francais eliront leur president les 18 avril et 2 mai 2027. a cinq mois du scrutin, Marine Le Pen et Jean-Luc Melenchon dominent les intentions de vote. Derriere eux, les candidatures se multiplient. Le Pen en tete, Melenchon profite de la dispersion La course est a deux vitesses. Dans le barometre Harris des 18 et 19 novembre, Marine Le Pen caracole a 31 % et Jean-Luc Melenchon suit a 18 %, dans une configuration ou Philippe et Attal sont tous deux en lice. Derriere, c'est l'embouteillage : Glucksmann et Lisnard devancent Philippe, tandis qu'Attal et Retailleau peinent a decoller. Le centre, lui, cherche toujours son champion. Philippe devisse. En avril, il atteignait 19 % dans un scenario ou il representait seul le centre ; en novembre, il ne recueille plus que 10 %. Melenchon suit la trajectoire inverse, passant de 12 a 19 %. Le Pen reste loin devant malgre un recul par rapport aux 35 a 36 % de debut novembre. Prudence cependant : l'ajout de nouveaux noms change les scenarios soumis aux sondes. La candidate du Rassemblement national (RN) conserve surtout un noyau fidele. Apres ses 23,15 % en 2022, 88 % de ses anciens electeurs envisagent encore de voter pour elle, selon Harris. Melenchon retrouve 74 % des siens. Leurs rivaux cherchent toujours des alliances. OpinionWay et YouGov racontent la meme histoire : Le Pen devance largement Melenchon. Mais l'affiche change les scores. Sans Attal, Lisnard ni Retailleau, YouGov les mesure a 40 % et 22 %. Ce grand ecart ne revele pas forcement des electeurs soudain convertis : il rappelle que retirer trois noms d'un questionnaire peut bousculer toute la course. Le Rassemblement national et La France insoumise (LFI) ont, eux, des bases solides. a droite, la primaire comme remede... et comme probleme La degringolade de Philippe est d'autant plus frappante qu'il fut longtemps presente comme l'heritier le mieux place du bloc presidentiel. La fin du second quinquennat d'Emmanuel Macron n'offre guere d'elan a ses successeurs : le barometre Ipsos de novembre ne mesure plus que 14 % d'opinions favorables au chef de l'etat. Le maire du Havre et fondateur d'Horizons refuse une primaire, et Gerald Darmanin, le ministre de la Justice, appelle a le soutenir. Pourtant, Gabriel Attal, Bruno Retailleau et David Lisnard tentent de bâtir une procedure commune . Leurs representants se sont reunis le 17 novembre autour d'une primaire ouverte, eventuellement electronique, les 31 janvier et 7 fevrier. Rien n'est definitivement arrete et Philippe etait absent. La primaire censee eviter la dispersion risque donc, s'il persiste, de l'officialiser. David Lisnard, maire de Cannes et chef de Nouvelle energie, atteint desormais 10 a 12 % dans certaines configurations et rivalise avec Philippe. Bruno Retailleau, patron des Republicains (LR), oscille entre 4 a 5 %. L'hypothese d'une grande primaire seduit 60 % des Francais interroges sur la question debut novembre. Encore faut-il definir qui pourrait y participer. Emmanuel Macron, prive de troisieme mandat consecutif, envisagerait selon la presse un front de Glucksmann a Lisnard. Aucun accord de cette ampleur n'existe. La gauche a choisi Glucksmann, pas l'unite Raphael Glucksmann, copresident de Place publique, gagne la primaire du 11 octobre avec 66,17 %, contre 14,46 % a Olivier Faure. « Ce soir, la bataille de France commence », lance-t-il. Mauvais souvenir : la bataille de France, en mai-juin 1940, s'est soldee par la defaite francaise face a l'Allemagne nazie. Dans les sondages, Glucksmann est credite de 11 a 12 %, loin derriere Melenchon. Glucksmann exclut une nouvelle alliance electorale avec LFI, mais Melenchon attire certains partisans de l'union. Le 18 novembre, Marine Tondelier, secretaire nationale des ecologistes, a declare sur France 2 : « Donc, moi je le dis tres clairement, je suis prete, et les ecologistes sont prets a travailler a une coalition autour de la candidature de Jean-Luc Melenchon. » Ce n'est pas un ralliement : les ecologistes voteront du 10 au 13 decembre sur leur strategie. Sandrine Rousseau, deputee ecologiste, soutient l'ouverture vers Melenchon. Yannick Jadot, candidat des Verts en 2022 et partisan de Glucksmann, a quitte Les ecologistes le 19 novembre. Le PS a suspendu ses discussions avec les Verts le 20 novembre. Le 21 novembre, Francois Ruffin a renonce a se presenter, faute d'une primaire de toute la gauche, sans soutenir de concurrent. Fabien Roussel, candidat du Parti communiste francais, se maintient malgre le soutien de neuf deputes communistes a Melenchon. Les candidatures encore en suspens La liste pourrait s'allonger. Francois Hollande entretient depuis plusieurs mois le suspense autour d'un eventuel retour a l'elysee. Redevenu depute de Correze, l'ancien president socialiste a de nouveau repousse sa decision le 19 novembre, laissant a Raphael Glucksmann le temps de demontrer qu'il peut atteindre le second tour. Selon LCP, Hollande attendrait desormais janvier pour trancher. Son entree en lice risquerait de compliquer davantage les calculs d'une gauche deja divisee. Au centre, c'est Christine Lagarde qui nourrit les speculations. L'ancienne ministre de l'economie a annonce qu'elle quitterait la presidence de la Banque centrale europeenne (BCE) le 7 fevrier 2027, neuf mois avant la fin de son mandat. De quoi relancer l'idee d'une candidature de recours, alors que Philippe et Attal reculent dans les sondages. Mais une autre destination est evoquee pour Lagarde : la presidence du Forum economique mondial de Davos. Elle n'a, a ce stade, pas annonce vouloir briguer l'elysee. L'interet qu'elle suscite depasse pourtant les conversations politiques. Selon le barometre Harris du 23 novembre, 29 % des Francais souhaitent qu'elle puisse se presenter, contre 32 % pour Hollande. Il ne s'agit pas d'intentions de vote, mais ces resultats montrent que leurs noms restent presents dans le debat. D'autres personnalites, comme Bruno Le Maire, Thierry Breton, elisabeth Borne, Matthieu Pigasse ou Xavier Bertrand, gardent egalement leurs options ouvertes. Cette reserve de pretendants pourrait offrir une solution aux partis en quete d'un profil rassembleur. Elle peut tout aussi bien accentuer une dispersion dont profitent deja les deux favoris. Les nouveaux venus et l'obstacle du second tour La liste des pretendants s'est de nouveau allongee. Le judoka Teddy Riner, candidat depuis le 9 novembre, recueille 4 a 5 % chez Harris. Dominique de Villepin s'est officiellement declare le 20 novembre, mais plafonne a 1 a 2 % dans les scenarios etudies. eric Zemmour se situe autour de 3 a 4 %. Marine Le Pen, elle, demeure dans la course malgre un pourvoi en cassation lie a sa condamnation dans l'affaire des assistants parlementaires europeens. Surtout, la domination du premier tour ne garantit pas a elle seule une victoire finale. Harris donne cependant Le Pen gagnante de tous les duels recemment testes : 65 % contre 35 % face a Melenchon dans l'enquete des 18 et 19 novembre ; 58 % contre 42 % face a Philippe et 60 % contre 40 % face a Glucksmann dans celle de debut novembre. Dans un duel Le Pen-Melenchon, 63 % des electeurs de Glucksmann au premier tour et 60 % de ceux de Philippe n'expriment pas de choix entre les finalistes. La campagne ne se reduit pas aux etiquettes Reste ce qui peut deplacer les lignes. Chez Harris, le pouvoir d'achat domine les priorites (59 %), devant la sante (40 %), l'immigration (36 %) et les retraites (31 %). L'Europe et la politique etrangere ne sont citees chacune que par 9 % des sondes. Ces sujets pourraient neanmoins peser dans un eventuel second tour, tant les orientations des principaux pretendants divergent sur l'Ukraine et les relations avec la Russie. Les alliances ne suffiront pas a repondre aux attentes. Ces sondages ne predisent rien : marges d'erreur et configurations comptent. etre teste dans une enquete ne vaut d'ailleurs ni investiture ni obtention des 500 parrainages d'elus requis pour se presenter a l'election presidentielle. Ils eclairent neanmoins une fracture. Le Pen et Melenchon disposent de socles identifiables ; leurs concurrents, eux, cherchent toujours comment transformer des electorats voisins en force commune. Les decisions des prochaines semaines peseront autant que les nouveaux sondages.

González había manifestado que pensaba votar en blanco. “Yo ya he votado. Soy una persona seria, no como otros”, ha respondido el expresidente. Este lunes, Pedro Sánchez ha anunciado que el PSOE incorporará a su programa electoral para las elecciones del 29-N un nuevo impuesto a los ultrarricos pensado para los patrimonios superiores a 100 millones de euros. Los socialistas recalcan que no afectará a las clases medias, a los ahorradores ni a los pequeños y medianos empresarios. items.title: Kebbi Information Commissioner petitions DSS over alleged abduction plot
items.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Kebbi State Commissioner for Information and Culture, Yakubu Ahmed-BK, has petitioned the Department of State Services (DSS) over alleged attempts by unidentified persons to abduct him and members of his family in Birnin Kebbi, the state capital. In a petition dated November 15, 2026, and addressed to the DSS Director-General through the Deputy Director-General, Operations, the commissioner alleged that the suspects were using a white, fully tinted Hilux or Innoson van with a red Agege registration number. A copy of the petition, made available to our correspondent on Monday, detailed two incidents in which the commissioner claimed the suspicious vehicle was sighted around locations connected to his movements and residence. Ahmed-BK said the first incident occurred on Tuesday, November 10, while he was taking his usual early-morning walk with his wife along the Sani Abacha Bypass in Birnin Kebbi. According to him, the occupants of the vehicle slowed down as they approached the couple and appeared to attempt to open one of its doors. He also claimed to have sighted what looked like the nozzle of a rifle inside the vehicle but could not clearly identify its occupants because of the tinted windows. He said the vehicle initially drove past them but later turned back and approached them slowly, prompting him and his wife to seek refuge inside Amina Rabo Plaza along the bypass. The commissioner said that after hiding for about five minutes, he cautiously checked outside and discovered that the vehicle was still parked nearby with its headlights on and engine running. He subsequently contacted a security officer attached to the Kebbi State Government House, identified as Alhaji Chika, who regularly encountered him during his morning exercise. Ahmed-BK said the officer immediately drove to the scene following his distress call, adding that the suspicious vehicle sped away upon his arrival. The commissioner said he initially considered the incident isolated until Sunday, November 15, when the same vehicle was allegedly sighted around his second residence in the Bayan Oando area of the state capital. He said residents spotted the vehicle between 6:30 a.m. and 7 a.m. and alerted another commissioner who also lives in the neighbourhood. According to him, the vehicle remained close to his residence for about five minutes before driving away. “Since the first incident of November 10, I have passed words about the matter to some neighbours and friends in the neighbourhoods. I must also state that since the first incident, I stopped going out for the trekking exercise altogether,” he said. Ahmed-BK expressed concern that the occupants might have been monitoring his movements and could have changed their approach after he stopped his regular morning walks. He therefore urged the DSS to investigate the incidents and deploy plain-clothes security personnel around his Bayan Oando residence to protect him and members of his family. He also requested surveillance operations to identify and track down the occupants of the vehicle. In addition, the commissioner appealed for permission, if legally permissible, to temporarily carry arms for personal protection until after the general elections. “I suggest that the road from ZBCC junction near Azbir Hotel up to Bayan Kara junction, all on Sani Abacha Bypass, be put under surveillance, especially between the hours of 6 a.m. and 7 a.m. when they seem to be active,” he added. The commissioner urged the DSS to respond promptly to his petition, expressing concern over the safety of his family. The petition did not indicate whether the DSS had responded to his request as of the time of filing this report. The post Kebbi Information Commissioner petitions DSS over alleged abduction plot appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Glovo déploie les agents de conformité terrain dans le cadre de son initiative Glovo 2030 pour la sécurité routière
items.description: Dans le cadre de son initiative Glovo 2030 pour la sécurité routière, objet d’une convention signée en février 2026 avec la NARSA, Glovo annonce le déploiement progressif de ses agents de conformité terrain, l’une des six actions prévues par ce programme. Après la numérotation des box de livraison, destinée à faciliter l’identification des livreurs, cette nouvelle action introduit une présence humaine de proximité, visant à accompagner les livreurs dans leurs activités quotidiennes, à favoriser le respect des règles de sécurité routière et à identifier et signaler les situations susceptibles de présenter des risques pour les livreurs et pour l’ensemble des usagers de la route. Des agents de proximité déployés au plus près des livreurs Déployé progressivement depuis le second trimestre 2026, le dispositif des agents de conformité terrain atteint aujourd’hui plus de 70 % de son objectif de déploiement, avec une présence dans une dizaine de villes du Royaume. Son organisation repose sur un maillage territorial adapté aux spécificités de chaque ville, tenant compte notamment du nombre de livreurs actifs, de la densité des commandes et de la concentration de l’activité dans les différentes zones, sans oublier les observations recueillies sur le terrain. Le ratio ciblé, selon les régions, est d’un agent de conformité terrain pour 100 à 150 livreurs. Les agents interviennent selon un système de rotation, afin de couvrir 22h sur les 24h, en cohérence avec les heures de livraison. La présence cible les zones de forte activité, notamment pendant les moments de forte affluence. Les agents de conformité terrain assurent une double mission : accompagner les livreurs dans la résolution de leurs difficultés quotidiennes mais aussi identifier et signaler les manquements constatés, qui seront traités et suivis d’actions de sensibilisation ou, selon leur gravité, de la rupture de la relation contractuelle avec le livreur indépendant concerné. Accompagner les livreurs et faciliter la résolution des difficultés sur le terrain Les agents de conformité terrain constituent un point de contact de proximité pour les livreurs lorsqu’ils rencontrent des difficultés dans le cadre de leur activité. Ils peuvent notamment intervenir pour faciliter la résolution de problèmes liés à l’application, aux commandes ou aux interactions avec les partenaires commerciaux. Ils assurent également un rôle de relais avec les Glovo Centers, structures locales chargées de la gestion opérationnelle des livreurs, afin de faciliter la prise en charge des difficultés signalées et d’améliorer la coordination entre les différents acteurs de l’écosystème. Cette présence humaine complète les dispositifs d’assistance existants en apportant une capacité d’écoute, d’orientation et d’accompagnement directement sur le terrain. Identifier et signaler les comportements non conformes pour permettre une réponse adaptée Les agents de conformité terrain ont également pour mission de repérer et de signaler les comportements susceptibles de mettre en danger les livreurs ou les autres usagers de la route. Leurs vérifications portent notamment sur le respect du code de la route, les manœuvres dangereuses et les comportements de conduite à risque en général ainsi que la conformité des équipements de protection et d’identification. Les situations observées sont documentées et transmises aux équipes compétentes pour examen et suivi. Selon la nature, la gravité ou la répétition des manquements confirmés, plusieurs niveaux d’actions sont prévus : La sensibilisation et le rappel des règles , pour expliquer les risques et les comportements attendus. La formation à la sécurité routière , permettant aux livreurs concernés de bénéficier d’un accompagnement spécifique en matière de code de la route. Les suspensions temporaires d’accès à la plateforme , en fonction de la nature et de la gravité des situations constatées. La rupture du contrat commercial avec le livreur auto-entrepreneur et la désactivation définitive du compte , dans les cas les plus graves, conformément aux dispositions contractuelles et aux procédures applicables. Les décisions sont prises après examen des situations signalées, dans le cadre d’un processus documenté prévoyant des possibilités de recours pour les livreurs indépendants concernés. Cette démarche vise à s’assurer que les prestations de livraison sont réalisées par les livreurs indépendants dans le respect de leurs engagements contractuels avec la plateforme, notamment en matière de sécurité routière. Une conduite dangereuse dans le cadre d’une livraison constitue ainsi un manquement aux obligations contractuelles du livreur auto-entrepreneur dans le cadre de la réalisation du service justifiant dans les cas les plus graves la résiliation du contrat commercial y afférent et la désactivation du compte associé. Un premier bilan : des milliers de vérifications et des centaines d’actions engagées Depuis le lancement des premières interventions, plus de 15 000 livreurs distincts ont fait l’objet de vérifications sur le terrain . Au total, plus de 335 000 vérifications de conformité ont été réalisées , permettant d’identifier différentes situations nécessitant un suivi ou une intervention. Sur le volet spécifique de la sécurité routière, plus de 3 600 livreurs ont été signalés pour des comportements de conduite à risque . Ces signalements ont notamment permis d’orienter les actions de sensibilisation et de formation. À ce jour, 850 livreurs ont bénéficié d’une formation à la sécurité routière dans le cadre du dispositif. Des séances de formation hebdomadaires sont planifiées pour couvrir à terme, l’ensemble des profils concernés. Les interventions ont également donné lieu à près de 190 suspensions temporaires et 250 désactivations définitives de comptes , à la suite de manquements confirmés. Ces premiers indicateurs témoignent de la mise en œuvre opérationnelle du dispositif, dont le déploiement se poursuit progressivement. Ils permettront également d’orienter les prochaines étapes de son développement, en fonction des besoins identifiés sur le terrain. Initiative Glovo 2030 pour la sécurité routière : six actions complémentaires pour une sécurité routière durable Pour rappel, l’Initiative Glovo 2030 prévoit le déploiement progressif de six actions complémentaires : la numérotation visible des sacs de livraison ; le déploiement des agents de conformité terrain ; la formation à la sécurité routière ; la création d’un canal de signalement destiné aux usagers de la route ; l’intégration d’outils télématiques ; le développement d’un Safety Score. Inscrites dans le cadre du partenariat conclu avec la NARSA, ces six actions traduisent trois priorités : mieux identifier, mieux prévenir et mieux responsabiliser. The post Glovo déploie les agents de conformité terrain dans le cadre de son initiative Glovo 2030 pour la sécurité routière appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Ndèye Fatou Mbodj Diattara, une consécration africaine à Nairobi
items.description: L'Administrateur général du FONGIP, Mme Ndèye Fatou MBODJ Diattara, a été honorée ce vendredi à Nairobi, au Kenya, parmi les 100 femmes les plus influentes d'Afrique en 2026. Cette distinction, décernée dans le cadre des African Women Awards, salue son parcours, son leadership et son engagement en faveur de l'autonomisation économique des femmes. À la réception de cette reconnaissance, elle a tenu à saluer le soutien des personnes ayant porté sa candidature, tout en associant le Président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, et l'ensemble du personnel du FONGIP à cette consécration. Elle a réaffirmé sa détermination à faire de l'accès au financement un instrument majeur de promotion de l'entrepreneuriat féminin et de l’emploi des jeunes. Une distinction qui consacre également le rayonnement du leadership féminin sénégalais à l'échelle continentale.

items.title: El Supremo aplica la amnistía a Puigdemont y cierra la causa del ‘procés’
items.description: Ahora sí: dos años y cinco meses después de la entrada en vigor de la ley de amnistía, el Tribunal Supremo se la ha aplicado plenamente a Carles Puigdemont, Toni Comín y Lluís Puig. La Sala Penal ha decretado este lunes el archivo definitivo del procedimiento en el que el expresidente de la Generalitat y los dos exconsejeros seguían procesados en rebeldía por un delito de malversación. Con el paso dado ahora, el Supremo termina de cumplir el mandato que le dio el Tribunal Constitucional el pasado 6 de octubre , cuando declaró que el alto tribunal debió otorgar la medida de gracia a los exdirigentes independentistas condenados o procesados por ese delito. items.title: Naqvi calls on PM Shehbaz as debate on new provinces gains steam
items.description: ISLAMABAD/LAHORE: Amid growing debate on the issue of creation of new provinces, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Monday called on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. According to an official handout from the Prime Minister Office (PMO), the interior minister met the prime minister in Islamabad and briefed him on the law and order situation in the country. The two also discussed the prevailing situation in the country, the statement said. Earlier in the day, Naqvi had met with Pakistan Muslim League-Quaid (PML-Q) chief Chaudhry Shujaat Hussain at his residence in Lahore. The debate over the creation of new provinces and devolution of powers came under discussion during the meeting. The meeting came amid an ongoing political debate over the creation of new provinces, with several political leaders pushing for a nationwide referendum to settle the matter. It was sparked by Naqvi’s July remarks, wherein he called for the formation of new administrative units in the country, saying the current “system” of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”. In Monday’s meeting, the two leaders discussed the overall political situation, measures to maintain law and order and the need to transfer power to the grassroots level, according to a statement issued by the interior ministry after the meeting. During the discussion, Shujaat said the question of creating new provinces was directly linked to public convenience, good governance, administrative efficiency and the country’s future. “Strengthening existing administrative units and making them more empowered can also be an effective way to address governance-related challenges. The biggest stakeholders of Pakistan are its ordinary people,” Shujaat was quoted as saying, adding that decisions should be made in accordance with the aspirations of the people. “If we do not take steps in the right direction today, tomorrow will not forgive us,” he remarked. Naqvi said it was imperative to take all decisions in accordance with the wishes of the people of Pakistan. The interior minister also briefed the PML-Q leader on the government’s counterterrorism and peacekeeping measures in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Minister for Overseas Pakistanis Chaudhry Salik Hussain and Punjab Minister for Industries Chaudhry Shafay Hussain were also present at the meeting. The meeting comes as Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry insisted last week that a referendum on the formation of new provinces “will happen” amid the debate on new provinces. In his remarks on Friday, Chaudhry had maintained that the PML-N would undertake “every last effort” to convince the PPP. “A referendum is neither non-constitutional nor undemocratic; the public’s opinion can be sought on any important matter,” he had said. Chaudhry’s remarks came after PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari delivered a no-holds-barred speech earlier last week that covered the question of new provinces. Bilawal had expressed his opposition to the creation of provinces and the idea of holding a referendum for such a move in his speech. He cautioned that any “forced” attempt to divide provinces, particularly in Sindh, could lead to bloodshed. However, the federal government maintains that a referendum is a legal and constitutional method of gauging public opinion on new provinces and that no political party should have reservations regarding it.

items.title: Abia Police condemn officers over pregnant woman’s hospital ordeal
items.description: By Steve Oko The Abia State Police Command has condemned the conduct of some of its personnel who allegedly stopped a man conveying his pregnant wife to hospital over the absence of a displayed vehicle number plate. The incident, captured in a viral video that has generated reactions on social media, involved officers attached to the Surveillance Patrol and Guard Team of Ubakala Divisional Police Station. The man was reportedly taking his pregnant wife to hospital after she began experiencing labour contractions when he encountered the officers, who allegedly insisted on taking him to the police station for driving without a displayed registration number plate. Reacting to the incident, the Police Command said it had identified the officers involved and commenced an investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the encounter and determine their level of responsibility. In a statement issued by the Police Public Relations Officer, Maureen Chinaka, the Command acknowledged that the man was driving without a displayed number plate, contrary to road traffic regulations. It explained that vehicle identification was important, particularly in view of prevailing security challenges, including vehicle theft and the use of unidentified vehicles for criminal activities. The Command, however, said enforcement of traffic regulations should be guided by sound judgment and consideration for human welfare, especially in emergency situations. On the claim that the man’s wife was in labour, the police said preliminary information indicated that she was fine and had not given birth as of the time of the statement. It added that no medical evidence had been presented to substantiate the claim that she was about to deliver. Despite this, the Command expressed displeasure over what it described as the officers’ apparent failure to demonstrate sufficient empathy towards the pregnant woman. The outgoing Commissioner of Police, AIG Wilfred Olutokunbo Afolabi, reiterated that the police had a statutory responsibility not only to prevent and detect crime and maintain law and order but also to protect lives, uphold citizens’ rights and assist people in distress. He stressed that police duties must be discharged with professionalism, empathy, restraint and respect for human dignity. According to him, although the Command would continue to enforce the law, such responsibilities must be carried out with humanity and consideration for prevailing circumstances. The Command assured members of the public that the investigation would be thorough and that appropriate disciplinary measures would be taken if misconduct was established. items.title: Plus d’une tonne de cocaïne interceptée, un réseau transnational démasqué
items.description: La police mauritanienne a annoncé, le samedi 21 novembre 2026, l’interception de 1 700 kilogrammes de cocaïne dans la région du Hodh Ech Chargui, à l’est du pays. Cette opération, menée après trois mois d’investigations, a permis de démanteler une partie d’un réseau international de trafic de drogue et de mettre la main sur deux suspects étrangers. C’est une prise d’une ampleur exceptionnelle que viennent de réaliser les services de sécurité mauritaniens. À l’issue de trois mois d’enquête, l’Office central de lutte contre les stupéfiants et les substances psychotropes a réussi à localiser un réseau criminel opérant dans plusieurs pays voisins et soupçonné de vouloir étendre ses activités sur le territoire mauritanien. Selon le communiqué de la police, les investigations, appuyées par des moyens modernes de surveillance et de suivi, ont conduit les enquêteurs jusqu’à la zone de «Daché», dans la région du Hodh Ech Chargui. Une équipe spécialisée y a intercepté un véhicule de marque Toyota Hilux transportant 1,7 tonne de cocaïne présentée comme étant de haute qualité. Deux ressortissants étrangers ont également été arrêtés lors de cette intervention. Les premières déclarations des mis en cause font état d’une cargaison provenant d’un pays voisin et destinée à un autre État frontalier. Son acheminement devait s’effectuer à travers plusieurs zones situées le long des frontières orientales et nord-orientales de la Mauritanie. Au terme de la procédure d’enquête, les deux suspects ainsi que la drogue saisie ont été présentés au parquet, le jeudi 19 novembre 2026. Parallèlement, les recherches se poursuivent pour retrouver trois autres individus de même nationalité, soupçonnés d'entretenir des liens directs avec le réseau. La police mauritanienne présente cette opération comme la plus importante saisie de cocaïne jamais réalisée, à ce jour, dans les pays de la sous-région. Une prise qui met en lumière l’ampleur des circuits transnationaux de narcotrafic et les tentatives d’implantation de leurs ramifications dans les pays sahéliens. Cette affaire intervient alors que l’Afrique de l’Ouest occupe une place croissante dans les circuits internationaux de la cocaïne. Entre les voies maritimes atlantiques, les installations portuaires et les corridors terrestres reliant les pays côtiers au Sahel, les réseaux criminels multiplient les itinéraires pour acheminer leurs cargaisons vers l’Afrique du Nord et l’Europe. Le Mali et le Niger figurent notamment parmi les territoires empruntés par ces circuits. Au-delà de l’importance de la quantité interceptée, cette saisie rappelle ainsi que la lutte contre le narcotrafic dans la région dépasse désormais les frontières nationales. La traque des trois suspects encore recherchés sera déterminante pour remonter davantage la chaîne de ce réseau et identifier l’ensemble de ses ramifications internationales. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Plus d'une tonne de cocaïne interceptée, un réseau transnational démasqué est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Attaque de drones ukrainiens en Libye : un navire militaire russe et un cargo visés à Benghazi
items.description: Dans la soiree du 22 novembre, les autorites libyennes ont rapporte une attaque de drones contre un navire militaire russe amarre dans le port de Benghazi, en Libye. D'apres leurs informations, l'explosion s'est produite sur le territoire d'une base militaire a l'aube du 22 novembre. Le gouvernement a charge les autorites competentes de mener une enquete approfondie et de coordonner leurs efforts avec la partie russe. Par la suite, des sources militaires de RT ont confirme l'attaque, precisant que l'Armee nationale libyenne avait empeche l'explosion de quatre des six drones de type bateau ukrainiens lors de l'assaut contre le navire russe. Selon les memes sources, les quatre drones interceptes appartenaient a la classe ukrainienne Magura. Les drones ont ete conserves et sont actuellement examines par des equipes techniques specialisees. Les interlocuteurs de RT, se referant aux resultats preliminaires de l'expertise, ont emis l'hypothese que les navires sans equipage auraient ete lances depuis une base navale ukrainienne situee dans l'ouest de la Libye. En outre, ils ont fait reference a des informations internationales anterieures faisant etat de la presence de bases et d'installations militaires ukrainiennes dans le pays, gerees par des militaires et des experts venus d'Ukraine. La diplomatie russe souligne le caractere terroriste de l'attaque Le meme jour, le correspondant de RT, Muhammad Al-Jazwi, a fait etat d'une nouvelle attaque dans la meme region, visant cette fois-ci un navire marchand battant pavillon maltais. D'apres des sources militaires, 21 drones sans equipage ont participe a la seconde frappe. Les forces armees libyennes ont reussi a en intercepter 17, mais l'un des drones a atteint sa cible. Plus tard, les interlocuteurs d'Al-Jazwi ont indique qu'au moins dix personnes, dont des ressortissants russes et libyens, avaient ete legerement blessees a la suite de l'attaque contre le navire russe. L'ambassadeur de Russie en Libye, Aïdar Aganine, a indique, lors d'un entretien avec RT, le caractere terroriste des attaques. Selon lui, les frappes contre des navires russes a Benghazi constituent une tentative de Kiev d'etendre le champ de la confrontation a des zones maritimes eloignees, ainsi que d'entraîner des etats tiers dans ses aventures, par l'intermediaire de protecteurs occidentaux qui apportent un soutien en matiere de renseignement et de logistique a de telles operations. Le diplomate russe a aussi ajoute que la partie russe etudierait les options de riposte possibles et ne laisserait pas les evenements sans reponse. Le Kremlin et le ministere russe de la Defense n'ont pour l'instant pas commente les evenements. Ce n'est pas la premiere attaque menee par le regime de Kiev loin du theâtre d'operations militaires. Le 4 mars, le methanier russe Arctic Metagaz a ete pris pour cible en Mediterranee. Moscou avait alors accuse Kiev et les services secrets britanniques d'avoir mene l'operation depuis les cotes libyennes. Plus tard en avril, RFI a mene une enquete qui a revele la presence de plus de 200 officiers et experts militaires ukrainiens dans l'ouest de la Libye, en coordination avec le gouvernement de Tripoli dirige par Abdelhamid Dbeibah. Selon l'agence de presse, les soldats sont repartis sur trois sites strategiques : le premier est situe a Misrata, le deuxieme a Zawia et le troisieme au quartier general de la 111e brigade, sur la route menant a l'aeroport de Tripoli.

items.title: Cyber Threats: CBN, NCC raise alarm over AI-powered attacks
items.description: By Babajide Komolafe The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) and the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) have raised the alarm over the growing threat of artificial intelligence-powered cyberattacks, warning that criminals are deploying sophisticated technology to defraud individuals, businesses and financial institutions. They spoke at the 2026 Annual Cybersecurity Conference of the Information Security Society of Africa-Nigeria (ISSAN) in Lagos, with the theme, “Cybersecurity: Balancing Risk, Resilience and Responsibility in the AI Era.” Speaking at the event, Director, Risk Management Department and Chief Risk Officer, CBN, Dr. Blaise Ijebor, said AI was lowering barriers to cybercrime by enabling criminals to execute sophisticated attacks at greater speed, scale and autonomy. “AI may be the greatest productivity tool ever given to cybercriminals,” he said, explaining that the technology could generate convincing phishing emails, clone voices, create synthetic faces and coordinate multiple stages of cyberattacks. Citing an investigation by AI company Anthropic, he said AI was estimated to have executed between 80 and 90 per cent of a reported cyber-espionage attack targeting about 30 organisations. To combat the threat, Ijebor urged financial institutions to strengthen identity verification, ensure that urgency does not override authentication, test backup systems and crisis response plans, and establish clear accountability for AI deployment. “AI is not the enemy of cybersecurity. Poorly governed AI is,” he said, advocating the use of AI to detect suspicious transactions, monitor abnormal behaviour and accelerate incident response. Representing the Executive Vice Chairman/Chief Executive Officer of NCC, Dr. Aminu Maida, the Director, Lagos Zonal Office, Mr. Tunji Jimoh, said vulnerabilities in telecommunications infrastructure could threaten financial services, healthcare, energy and other critical sectors. He disclosed that the commission introduced a Cyber Resilience Framework for the telecommunications sector in February 2026, with supplementary implementation guidance released in August, targeting full industry compliance within 12 months. He urged operators to implement zero-trust security principles, continuous threat monitoring, incident reporting and stronger cybersecurity governance, including across third-party technology providers. President, Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria (CIBN), Dr. Dele Alabi, called on bank boards to invest in cyber resilience, management teams to integrate cyber risks into enterprise-wide decisions, and employees to strictly observe security protocols. He also advocated stronger partnerships and intelligence sharing among industry stakeholders. ISSAN President, Dr. David Isiavwe, urged organisations to improve incident reporting and share indicators of compromise, warning that Nigeria might be capturing fewer than half of actual cyber incidents. He said collective responsibility, professional competence and collaboration were essential to protecting trust in the digital economy. The post Cyber Threats: CBN, NCC raise alarm over AI-powered attacks appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Yamal out of Barcelona’s Champions League trip to Sabah
items.description: Lamine Yamal will not travel with his Barcelona team-mates to take on Sabah in the Champions League due to an ankle problem, the Catalan giants said on Monday. Star forward Yamal is being left at home “as a precaution” due to “discomfort in his right ankle” picked up during Sunday’s exciting 3-2 win over Villarreal. The 19-year-old will be available for Barca’s La Liga fixture against Deportivo La Coruna this coming weekend, Barca confirmed. Hansi Flick’s side currently sit three points ahead of Real Madrid at the top of La Liga and are on course to automatically qualify for the last 16 of the Champions League ahead of Wednesday’s match in Azerbaijan. items.title: 2027: We’re not jittery; opposition not ready – Bwala
items.description: Sekinat Osundiji Presidential spokesman Daniel Bwala has said the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) is not worried about the opposition ahead of the 2027 general election, insisting that its political rivals are not prepared for the contest. Bwala, Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Policy Communication, stated this during an interview on Channels Television, where he dismissed suggestions that the ruling party was apprehensive about the growing activities of opposition parties. He said the APC was confident about its political standing, adding that the opposition was not ready for the election. “I do not think the opposition is ready. Those who understand the political trajectory can see that they are already facing defeat,” Bwala said. His comments followed questions about President Tinubu’s decision to expand his campaign itinerary beyond the initial 12 states, amid reports of attacks on campaign materials and the president’s convoy. Defending the adjustment, Bwala described it as a strategic decision rather than an indication that the APC was worried about its political opponents. “President Tinubu is not scared. It is a matter of strategy. He is a chess player, who studies the moves of his opponents before deciding on his next move,” he said. He, however, acknowledged that the ruling party was working to secure voters’ support, saying it would be wrong to assume that Nigerians had already decided to re-elect the president. “We are not worried, but we are working hard because we respect the will of the people. We cannot take their votes for granted,” Bwala said. On the political situation in the North, Bwala described the region as a major battleground in the 2027 election, noting that the president’s campaign activities there were part of a deliberate strategy. He rejected suggestions that the North was united against Tinubu, arguing that the position of individual political leaders should not be interpreted as the collective position of the region. “There is no unanimous adoption of a candidate by any bloc in Nigeria, not even in the North. The position of one political leader should not be taken as the position of the entire region,” he said. Bwala also argued that the president had made significant efforts in the South-West, which informed his decision to concentrate more campaign activities in other regions. Addressing Peter Obi’s performance in the 2023 presidential election, the presidential spokesman said the Labour Party candidate benefited from religious sentiments surrounding the APC’s Muslim-Muslim presidential ticket. “Politics is about strategy. In 2023, Peter Obi benefited from the reaction of some Christians to the APC’s Muslim-Muslim ticket. That was one of the factors that shaped the election,” Bwala said. He further claimed that Obi had visited 12 major churches during the previous election cycle but had not maintained the same pattern ahead of 2027. Bwala alleged that some churches had declined Obi’s requests to attend their services, arguing that the strategy he adopted in 2023 was no longer playing out in the same way. He also questioned Obi’s current political standing, claiming that several prominent stakeholders who supported him in 2023 had since left his political camp. On the opposition’s preparedness, Bwala criticised its political strategy and questioned the policy proposals of some of its leading figures. He specifically faulted Obi for allegedly lacking a manifesto, while acknowledging that the New Democratic Congress (NDC) had published a campaign blueprint. The presidential spokesman also cited data analytics he said were conducted recently, claiming that positive mentions of Tinubu were twice those recorded for each of the other presidential candidates. According to him, a prominent ADC member who supports former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar shared the findings with him. He, however, did not disclose the individual’s identity or the methodology used in the analysis. On the contest in the North-East, Bwala said the APC expected to win Borno State but anticipated a contest with Atiku in Adamawa State, the former vice-president’s home state. “We will win Borno State, although Adamawa may be more competitive because it is Atiku Abubakar’s home state,” he said. The post 2027: We’re not jittery; opposition not ready – Bwala appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 2027: Obi’s camp alleges plot to link him with IPOB
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The camp of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has alleged a plot by some political actors to link him with the Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) in a campaign it claims is aimed at weakening his growing support in Northern Nigeria. The Peter Obi Media Office (POMR) raised the alarm on Monday, alleging that individuals within the ruling party and some opposition elements were coordinating a propaganda campaign to portray the former Anambra State governor as sympathetic to Biafran separatism. In a statement signed by its spokesperson, Idris Zekeri, the media office said the alleged campaign was intended to discourage Northern Nigerians, particularly young people, from supporting the Obi-Kwankwaso political movement. It alleged that the campaign could involve sponsored reports in Northern newspapers, interviews on radio stations in the region and coordinated narratives on social media. The media office also cited a claim by a social media personality, Gucci Commando, who allegedly said he had visited IPOB leader, Nnamdi Kanu, in Sokoto and attributed political endorsements in support of Obi to him. However, POMR described the claim as questionable, insisting that allegations of such magnitude required independent verification and should not be presented as established facts. The statement read in part: “The Peter Obi Media Office has expressed grave concern about credible intelligence indicating that certain actors within the ruling party, together with elements of the opposition, have hatched a coordinated anti-Obi propaganda effort aimed at exploiting Nigeria’s delicate ethnic and security divisions. “The alleged purpose of this effort is to falsely link Peter Obi to Biafran separatism and depict him as politically aligned with IPOB leader Nnamdi Kanu, apparently to distance Northern Nigerians, especially young people, from the Obi-Kwankwaso political movement.” The media office maintained that Obi was neither an ethnic nor a religious candidate, describing him as a Nigerian whose political vision and aspirations extended beyond ethnic, religious and regional divisions. It said his political objective was to address the country’s economic, security and governance challenges and build a nation that served the interests of all Nigerians. Zekeri said Obi’s commitment to justice, dialogue, national reconciliation and the rule of law should not be misrepresented as support for separatism. He urged Northern Nigerians not to allow what he described as political propaganda to undermine relationships built around the shared aspiration for a better country. “The Obi-Kwankwaso political engagement is a national initiative, not an ethnic enterprise,” he said. The media office also called on those making allegations linking Obi to separatist activities to provide verifiable evidence rather than rely on insinuations. It urged media organisations, particularly Northern newspapers and radio stations, to independently verify political claims and reject attempts to use them to promote divisive narratives. POMR said Nigeria’s challenges, including poverty, insecurity, unemployment, inadequate education and healthcare, required serious national attention rather than what it described as ethnic suspicion and religious manipulation. It added that Obi’s political constituency remained Nigeria and that his commitment was to the well-being of all Nigerians. The post 2027: Obi’s camp alleges plot to link him with IPOB appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Rencontres de Bamako : Quelle vitrine pour les photographes maliens ?
items.description: © Internet À quelques jours de l’ouverture des Rencontres de Bamako, la présence des artistes maliens dans la sélection officielle donne une visibilité particulière à la création locale. Reste à savoir comment cette exposition internationale peut se prolonger en reconnaissance professionnelle et rapprocher davantage la photographie de son public à Bamako. La 15 ème édition de la Biennale africaine de la photographie se tiendra du 26 novembre au 26 janvier autour du thème « Refabulation(s) ». Sur les 49 artistes retenus, 7 ont un lien déclaré avec le Mali, parmi lesquels Fatoumata Diabaté, John Kalapo, Aïssata Kané, Alfousseny Konaté et Oumou Traoré. La sélection résulte d’un appel international ouvert aux photographes et artistes visuels du continent et de la diaspora. Les propositions ont notamment été appréciées en fonction de leur relation avec le thème et de la démarche artistique développée. Pour les Maliens retenus, l’exposition offre une occasion de présenter leurs travaux devant des professionnels, commissaires, institutions et visiteurs venus de différents pays. John Kalapo, déjà présent lors de précédentes éditions, y voit un cadre important pour la scène photographique. « La Biennale africaine de la photographie joue un rôle essentiel dans la promotion de la créativité photographique, en soutenant la recherche, l’innovation et l’affirmation de nouvelles écritures visuelles », estime-t-il. Public La visibilité des artistes ne dépend toutefois pas uniquement du regard des professionnels étrangers. La fréquentation des expositions par le public malien constitue également une dimension importante de cette édition. Selon Tidiane Sangaré, Directeur général de la Maison africaine de la photographie, un programme de médiation doit mobiliser les écoles de formation artistique, les universités et les lycées. L’Institut national des Arts et le Conservatoire Balla Fasséké Kouyaté figurent parmi les établissements particulièrement ciblés. Le dispositif doit accompagner les visiteurs pendant les deux mois d’exposition. Une quinzaine de lieux privés sont également annoncés dans le programme « Off », en complément des principaux sites de la Biennale. Pour les photographes maliens, cette présence dans la programmation constitue une étape. La suite se joue aussi dans les rencontres professionnelles, les possibilités d’exposition après Bamako et la capacité à se construire un public local régulier autour de leurs œuvres. Ali Sankaré
